newsitem.title: UK: Marketing seen key to UK mobile 'phone success.
newsitem.headline: Marketing seen key to UK mobile 'phone success.

text.p: Marketing skills are likely to determine the success of Britain's four mobile telephone companies as attempts to woo more customers might bring prices and revenues down, some telecoms analysts said on Tuesday.

Andrew Harrington, analyst at Salomon Brothers, says that in about one year the four mobile phone operators -- Vodafone Group Plc, Cellnet, majority-owned by British Telecommunications Plc, Orange Plc and Cable and Wireless Plc's One-2-One cellular unit -- will be selling essentially the same product.
"Therefore it's a marketing and product positioning game at which Orange has been spectacularly good in the past -- but the other guys are all catching up," he added.
Orange hopes to introduce dual band handsets by April or May that can operate at both 1800 and 900 Mhz. But the company concedes that its rivals are likely to offer the same service next year.

Strong retained revenue figures for subscribers from Orange were brushed aside by some who said that in order to increase market penetration to high Scandinavian levels, revenues would have to fall by around a third.
"Overall revenue growth in the UK market is slowing," said Harrington, adding that investment risk across the UK cellular market was increasing as the predictability of revenues and profits declines.
Scandinavia, where more than 25 percent of the population use mobile 'phones, is a favourite example for the growth potential of the industry.
But growth there has been led by a falling prices of handsets and annual tariffs.

However, analysts agree with companies such as Orange that subscriber numbers can only go one way -- upwards. With a market penetration of only around 11.7 percent, Britain lags Scandinavia, Australia and the U.S.
Analysts expect overall subscribers to rise around 80 percent to 12.2 million by the beginning of the next century.

The sudden departure of Cellnet's managing director Howard Ford, announced on Tuesday in a curt statement by BT, was put by some newspapers down to unease about the performance of the UK's second biggest mobile operator.
Cellnet, 40-percent owned by Securicor Group Plc, announced last month that it had connected 2.68 million customers, narrowing the gap with Vodafone. It has more than one million digital customers.
BT stated only that Ford, who had been with the company for less than three years, had decided to pursue his career outside the BT Group.
